subject: Biology
title: Neuroglial Support Network & Blood-Brain Barrier
learningObjectives: Differentiate the 5 neuroglial cell types by developmental origin, anatomical location, and function
Describe the cellular composition and barrier mechanics of the Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB)
Contrast CNS myelination by Oligodendrocytes with PNS myelination by Schwann Cells
content:
Neuroglia are non-excitable supporting cells that outnumber neurons by $10:1$ in the central nervous system.

```
                             NEUROGLIAL CELL TYPES
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                             ▼                             ▼
  ASTROCYTES (CNS)              OLIGODENDROCYTES (CNS)       SCHWANN CELLS (PNS)
  ├── Forms Blood-Brain Barrier ├── Myelinates MULTIPLE       ├── Myelinates SINGLE
  └── K⁺ Homeostasis                CNS axons simultaneously     PNS axon segment
                                                                 └── Forms Neurilemma
```

### 2.1 Neuroglial Cells Matrix

| Glial Cell Type | Anatomical Location | Developmental Origin | Primary Physiological Role |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Astrocytes** | Central Nervous System (CNS) | Ectodermal | Star-shaped cells; perivascular feet form the **Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB)**; regulates extracellular $\text{K}^+$ concentrations and recycles neurotransmitters |
| **Oligodendrocytes** | Central Nervous System (CNS) | Ectodermal | Synthesizes **Myelin Sheaths** around **multiple CNS axons** simultaneously; lacks neurilemma *(No regeneration in CNS)* |
| **Schwann Cells** | Peripheral Nervous System (PNS) | Neural Crest (Ectodermal) | Wraps around **PNS axons** to form the **Myelin Sheath** and outer **Neurilemma (Sheath of Schwann)**; drives PNS axon regeneration |
| **Microglia** | Central Nervous System (CNS) | **Mesodermal** (Unique!) | Specialized resident macrophages of the CNS; phagocytoses cellular debris and pathogens |
| **Ependymal Cells** | CNS (Ventricular Lining) | Ectodermal | Simple ciliated columnar epithelium lining brain ventricles and spinal central canal; forms **Choroid Plexus** to secrete **Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF)** |

conceptBreakdown.heading: Blood-Brain Barrier Tight Junctions
conceptBreakdown.explanation: The Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) is formed by continuous brain capillary endothelial cells joined by high-resistance Zonula Occludens (tight junctions), surrounded by a basal lamina and astrocyte end-feet (podocytes), restricting polar and macromolecular diffusion.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Multiple Sclerosis vs Guillain-Barré Syndrome
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune demyelinating disease targeting Oligodendrocytes in the CNS. Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS) is an autoimmune demyelinating polyneuropathy targeting Schwann Cells in the PNS.
